1. Vide this order, this court shall dispose off the present appeal preferred against the impugned orders dated 20.10.2022 and 19.10.2023, passed by the court of Ld.
MM-01, North District, Rohini Courts, Delhi in Complaint Case No. 5292915/2016,
titled as 'State Vs. Mehtab' whereby the appellant was sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of two months for the offence u/s 304A IPC and simple imprisonment for a period of two weeks for offence u/s 279 IPC.

The FIR was registered u/s 279/304A IPC and u/s 146/196 Motor Vehicle Act.
The investigation was carried out.
The appellant/accused was SATISH KUMAR KUMAR 2024.02.16 14:20:51 +0530 arrested.
The offending vehicle i.e. tractor bearing registration No.DL-1E-2175 was recovered.

After completion of investigation, the charge-sheet was filed against the appellant and notice u/s 251 Cr.P.C. vide order dated 23.03.2016 was served upon the appellant to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

After concluding the trial, the accused was convicted and aggrieved against the said impugned judgment dated 20.10.2022 and impugned order on sentence dated 19.10.2023, the present appeal has been filed on the ground that the prosecution has miserably failed to prove its case beyond all reasonable doubts against the appellant and the ld.
Trial court has passed the judgment in haste without appreciating the evidence led by the prosecution.

By way of the present appeal, it is prayed that the impugned judgement dated 20.10.2022 and order on sentence dated 19.10.2023 may kindly be set aside and the appeal filed by the appellant may kindly be allowed.
3. That, notice of this appeal was served upon the State and ld.

APP for the State has submitted that he does not want to file reply of the appeal and has argued straightaway and submitted that PW1 Meghnath who is the eye-witness and sustained the injuries has proved its case against the appellant beyond all reasonable doubts.

It has also been submitted by ld. APP for the Digitally Crl. Revision No.261/2023 signed by SATISH SATISH KUMAR KUMAR Date:

State that the sentence is only upto 2 months and as per the provisions of Section 376 sub clause (b) of Cr.P.C., the sentence which was awarded less than three months and against that the appeal is not maintainable.
4. Ld. counsel for the appellant has submitted that the appellant belongs to poor strata of the society and is plying the E- Rikshaw.

The prosecution has not been able to prove its case against the appellant beyond all reasonable doubts and make a submission that the appeal may kindly be allowed and the impugned judgement dated 20.10.2022 and order on sentence dated 19.10.2023 may kindly be set aside.

5. Having heard the submissions made by ld. counsel for the appellant as well as Ld. Additional Public Prosecutor for the State/respondent and after going through the averments of the appeal and also after going through the trial court record as well as the impugned judgement dated 20.10.2022 and impugned order on sentence dated 19.10.2023 passed by the ld.

After going through the testimony of the other material witnesses, this court is of the considered that there is no irregularity or illegality in the impugned judgment passed by the ld.

That, this court is also of the considered view that the convicted has been awarded sentence only for a period of two months for the offence u/s 304A and simple imprisonment for a period of four weeks for the offence u/s 279 IPC and the appeal where the sentence is awarded upto three months is not maintainable.

Section 376 of Cr.P.C. is reproduced as under :-
"Section 376 of Cr.P.C. :-No Appeal in petty cases.

Notwithstanding anything contained in section 374, there shall be no appeal by a convicted person in any of the following cases, namely-- a) ....
b) where a Court of Session or a Metropolitan Magistrate passes only a sentence of imprisonment for a term not exceeding three months or of fine not exceeding two hundred rupees, or of both such imprisonment and fine."
